task.description: Validate CODE-DESIGNER's design at lib/letflow/design/req051-parallel-gateway-split-join.md against REQ-051's 6 acceptance criteria (see handoffs/WF02-REQ051-20260818/step-01-code-designer.json's task.description/acceptance_criteria for the full requirement text). Key mechanisms to verify independently: (1) branch_id scheme (parent_token_id <> "/" <> declaration_order_index) actually produces N distinct branch_ids deterministically and purely; (2) new JoinCounter struct + InstanceState.join_counters field is genuinely pure data, no process/GenServer; (3) the new cancelled-branch representation ({:cancel_branch, branch_id} event + cancelled_branches MapSet) is entirely this requirement's own -- confirm it does NOT silently assume REQ-052 exists; (4) join_outcome/1's :wait|:fire|:cancel_join set-algebra (expected - (received ∪ cancelled)) correctly implements all-cancelled -> :cancel_join -> instance CANCELLED, and fire-exactly-once under any arrival order; (5) REQ-049's VariableMerge.merge/3 is genuinely reused, not reimplemented.
acceptance_criteria: Every one of REQ-051's 6 acceptance criteria maps to a concrete design element -- verify by direct cross-reference, not by trusting the design doc's own traceability claims.
The cancelled-branch representation is genuinely self-contained (no unstated dependency on REQ-052).

join_outcome/1's logic is checked against edge cases: 0 branches cancelled+all received (fire), all cancelled (cancel_join), a mix (fire once remaining active arrive), concurrent/reordered arrival (still exactly-once).
REQ-049's merge function is called, not duplicated.
No implementation code in the design artifact.
The 8 listed open questions are genuinely non-blocking for ELIXIR-DEV, or if any IS blocking, this is a FAIL requiring CODE-DESIGNER to resolve it.

The MINOR issue CODE-DESIGNER flagged (req049-variable-scoping-merge.md vs actual req049-variable-merge.md filename in its own artifacts_in) doesn't indicate the design was built against the wrong/nonexistent file.

result.summary: Independently verified lib/letflow/design/req051-parallel-gateway-split-join.md against REQ-051's 6 acceptance criteria (step-01 handoff's task.acceptance_criteria), cross-checked against the shipped lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex, instance_state.ex, token.ex, and req049-variable-merge.md's actual merge/3 @spec. All 7 gate checks pass. (1) Traceability table §11 maps every AC to a concrete design element -- verified directly, not by trusting the table: split id/branch_id derivation (§3.1) is deterministic (parent_token_id<>"/"<>declaration-order-index, never edge.id, correctly justified since no CHK-01..CHK-08 check enforces edge-id uniqueness) and produces N distinct branch_ids by construction; JoinCounter (§2) is a plain defstruct with MapSet fields, stored in a new InstanceState.join_counters :: map() field -- genuinely pure data, no process/GenServer anywhere. (2) Cancelled-branch representation is self-contained: {:cancel_branch, branch_id} is a new transition_event/0 constructor fully handled inside transition.ex itself (§3.4); §8 explicitly states 'None on REQ-052' and REQ-052 is named only as a forward dependent (its future cancel_instance/N path will emit these events into this same entry point) -- no alias/call into any REQ-052 module, matching REQ-044/049's own precedent for similar non-dependencies. (3) join_outcome/1's set algebra (still_outstanding = expected - (received union cancelled)) verified by hand against all 4 required edge cases: 0-cancelled-all-received -> still_outstanding empty, received non-empty -> :fire (correct); all-cancelled-zero-arrived -> still_outstanding empty, received empty -> :cancel_join -> instance :cancelled (correct, EE-07 AC4); mixed (2 arrived, 1 cancelled of 3) -> :fire, matching AC2/AC3's 'does not wait for the cancelled branch' (correct); reordered/any arrival order -> MapSet union/difference are order-independent by definition, and Map.delete on every :fire/:cancel_join outcome (both call sites) makes a second resolution of the same cohort impossible (any later event referencing that branch_id fails at find_token, since cancellation/arrival both remove the token from instance_state.tokens on resolution) -- exactly-once confirmed by construction, not merely asserted. (4) REQ-049 reuse verified against the actual merge/3 @spec read directly from req049-variable-merge.md: call shape VariableMerge.merge(instance_state.variables, %{}, nil) matches the real (current_variables, incoming_variables, variable_validations) parameter order; per req049 §9 this is a legitimate no-op given InstanceState has no per-branch variable overlay -- no second collision rule is defined anywhere in this module (grep-verifiable), and merge_event() is reused verbatim in pending_event/0 rather than re-shaped. (5) No implementation code: every code block in the design doc is @type/@spec/defstruct only, no function body/case/cond with real logic -- consistent with the accepted precedent already set by req044-transition-kernel.md and req049-variable-merge.md (both shipped, status: done). (6) All 8 open questions (12.1-12.5 plus 3.2/3.3/4.1's inline flags) reviewed individually: none leaves an implementation decision unspecified -- each documents a concrete, deterministic design choice (e.g. 12.1's single-cohort-per-join-node key with explicit overwrite-on-reentry behavior, 12.2's named :combined_split_join_not_supported error, 12.5's concrete no-op call site) and flags it for REVIEWER/RELEASE-VALIDATOR re-verification against unreachable R-Co source rather than leaving ELIXIR-DEV to guess -- none is blocking. (7) The MINOR filename issue is not a wrong-file problem: confirmed lib/letflow/design/req049-variable-merge.md is the real, existing file (ls verified) and its actual merge/3 signature matches exactly what this design's §4.3 step 1 calls -- the handoff's artifacts_in typo (req049-variable-scoping-merge.md) does not indicate the design was built against a nonexistent or wrong document.
